scope: Qwen3 1.7B runs underlying the recent Hard66 charts; no new inference was performed.
method: Screened saved reasoning text for explicit memory claims, Bible/book references, and outside-looking names/details; manually compared candidate findings with question, choices, and local verse excerpts reconstructed from the saved files and the runner verse-window function. This is a qualitative screen, not a causal test or a fully adjudicated prevalence estimate.
unavailable_traces: The older clean, omission, mistranslation, and Google WBW thinking runs retained thinking lengths but no text; no reasoning text was found in their campaign logs. Grammar 5–30% has one failed MCQ generation without a saved trace.
conclusion: There is evidence of unsupported biblical associations in the saved traces, including a Babylonian-exile identification in an open-ended answer and unsupported genealogy in an MCQ trace. These findings do not establish accurate Bible recall, the true internal source of the additions, or a causal benefit to MCQ accuracy.
